# Abstract

Drought stress can affect crop growth and productivity. This project analyses public RNA-seq expression data from two rice cultivars, IR64 and N22, using the NCBI GEO accession GSE183894. The supplementary data contain FPKM expression values for control and drought-treated seedlings. The workflow includes data import, preprocessing, exploratory quality checks, visualisation and differential expression analysis using limma on log2-transformed FPKM values. The final results and biological interpretation must be completed from the outputs generated by the scripts.

# Introduction

Describe the agricultural importance of drought stress, the relevance of rice, the contrasting cultivars, research question, aim and objectives. Cite the GEO study and relevant literature.

# Data

The dataset is GSE183894 from NCBI GEO (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE183894). The organism is *Oryza sativa*. GEO sample records describe 21-day-old seedlings treated for six hours, using reverse-osmosis water as control and 20% PEG 6000 as drought treatment. Supplementary files contain tab-delimited FPKM values.

```{r data-summary}
if (file.exists("../data/processed/sample_metadata.rds")) {
  meta <- readRDS("../data/processed/sample_metadata.rds")
  print(meta)
} else {
  cat("Run code/01_download_geo_data.R and code/02_prepare_expression.R first.")
}
```

# Methods

Explain GEOquery download, file inspection, metadata parsing, gene matrix construction, quality control, log2(FPKM + 1) transformation and the limma workflow. State clearly that FPKM is not raw count data and that DESeq2/voom were not applied.

# Results

Complete this section after running the pipeline. Include actual sample and gene counts, QC observations, significant-gene counts and selected gene tables. Do not invent values.

# Discussion

Interpret actual findings. Discuss candidate genes only after checking gene annotations and relevant literature. Distinguish the two within-cultivar contrasts from a formal genotype-by-treatment interaction test. Address limited replication, FPKM limitations and PEG treatment as a drought simulation.

# Conclusion

Summarise the analysis and evidence-supported findings. Avoid claiming that any gene causes drought tolerance.

# Reproducibility

List R version, package versions, execution order and GEO accession. The scripts in `code/` reproduce the download, preprocessing, visualisations and statistical analysis. Save `sessionInfo()` after the final run.
